title: Reduction of the actual unbounded integral projection morphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, the constant finite quotient ring sheaf, for a fixed $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$, $D_S(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{S_T})$ of internal module objects, the derived module pullback and pushforward with their derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the uncompleted relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Set $D_{n,T}K=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the derived scalar extension of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism. Use $L_{f,R}\dashv F_{f,R}$ and $L_{f,S}\dashv F_{f,S}$ and precisely the comparisons $\lambda_f,\rho_{f,n}$ of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison]. Let $\pi^R_{f,K,M}$ and $\pi^S_{f,U,V}$ be the actual module-object projection morphisms, namely the adjuncts of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)t_f$, where $t_f:L_f(F_fK\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_fF_fK\otimes L_fM$ is the canonical derived pullback-tensor map [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map, def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Let
$$b_{T,U,V}:D_{n,T}(U\otimes^L_{R_T}V)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{n,T}U\otimes^L_{S_T}D_{n,T}V$$
be the canonical derived scalar-tensor balancing map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], normalized on flat-term K-flat representatives by $(u\otimes v)\otimes s\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes s)$.

For every $K\in D_R(X)$ and $M\in D_R(Y)$ the following equality holds in $D_S(Y)$:
$$\begin{aligned}
&\pi^S_{f,D_{n,X}K,D_{n,Y}M}\circ(\rho_{f,n,K}\otimes1)\circ b_{Y,F_{f,R}K,M}\\
&=F_{f,S}\bigl((1\otimes\lambda_{f,M}^{-1})\circ b_{X,K,L_{f,R}M}\bigr)\circ\rho_{f,n,K\otimes L_{f,R}M}\circ D_{n,Y}(\pi^R_{f,K,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
Its source is $D_{n,Y}(F_{f,R}K\otimes^L_{R_Y}M)$ and its target is $F_{f,S}(D_{n,X}K\otimes^L_{S_X}L_{f,S}D_{n,Y}M)$. Thus these specified comparisons identify the reduction of the actual integral projection map with the quotient-coefficient projection map, naturally in both inputs. No properness, completeness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of the projection map is assumed.

proof.text: Use the internal/section equivalences at $R_T$ and $S_T$. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] they preserve flat-term K-flat complexes and identify balanced tensors by the identity on local pure tensors. By [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] they identify the specified unbounded pull-push adjunctions, including their counits. By [lem-pd-section-derived-tensor-normalization] the actual module-object pullback tensor map becomes the canonical ringed tensor map. Scalar extension and its $S_T$-action are identified as well: the balanced tensor with $S_T$ is sent to the same balanced tensor, with $s'$ acting on its $S_T$ factor. Thus the specified formulas for $b$ and $\lambda$ become precisely the sectionwise formulas, on K-flat representatives and hence in the derived categories. It suffices to prove the equality there and carry it back through these equivalences.

proof.text: Abbreviate $D_{n,T}$ to $D_T$ and suppress $f$ in $L_R,F_R,L_S,F_S,\lambda,\rho$. Consider the ringed-topos square with vertical morphisms $(T,S_T)\to(T,R_T)$ given by the identity topos and $R_T\to S_T$, and horizontal morphisms induced by $f$. The ring maps in its two composites coincide: both are the quotient map pulled from the point, because the structural maps $\alpha_f:f^{-1}(\Lambda_Y)\to\Lambda_X$ are by definition the components at $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and $\Lambda=A/\pi^n$ of one natural isomorphism $f^*p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], so they commute with $p^*$ of the quotient $\mathcal O_E\to A/\pi^n$. The scalar/pullback comparison $L_SD_Y\to D_XL_R$ is the composition comparison around this square. Its flat-term K-flat formula is exactly $f^{-1}(x\otimes s)\mapsto f^{-1}x\otimes f^{-1}s$, so it is the particular $\lambda$ of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison]. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the two composites and their identical structural ring map. It gives monoidality of this comparison, without requiring flatness of $R_T\to S_T$.

proof.text:
Write $t_R,t_S$ for the two pullback tensor maps. The monoidality just obtained says, for $U,V\in D_R(Y)$,
$$b_{X,L_RU,L_RV}\circ D_X(t_{R,U,V})\circ\lambda_{U\otimes V}
=(\lambda_U\otimes\lambda_V)\circ t_{S,D_YU,D_YV}\circ L_S(b_{Y,U,V}).\tag{*}$$
Indeed, the tensorator of $L_SD_Y$ is $t_S\circ L_S(b_Y)$ and that of $D_XL_R$ is $b_X\circ D_X(t_R)$. The scalar tensorator here is the specified $b$: both normalized maps send $(u\otimes v)\otimes s$ to $(u\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes s)$. Thus (*) specializes the monoidal composition equation of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] with these tensorators. There is no permutation of the homogeneous variables and hence no extra Koszul sign.

proof.text:
Put $C=F_RK$, $W=C\otimes^L_{R_Y}M$, $H=K\otimes^L_{R_X}L_RM$, and
$$q=(1\otimes\lambda_M^{-1})\circ b_{X,K,L_RM}:D_XH\longrightarrow D_XK\otimes^L_{S_X}L_SD_YM=:Z.$$
For $a:D_YW\to F_SZ$ write $a^\flat=\varepsilon^S_Z\circ L_S(a)$. The adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] makes this operation a bijection. From the defining adjunct of $\rho$ in [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison] we have, for every $J\in D_R(X)$,
$$\varepsilon^S_{D_XJ}\circ L_S(\rho_J)=D_X(\varepsilon^R_J)\circ\lambda_{F_RJ}.\tag{**}$$
This follows by applying the Hom bijection to its own inverse; it does not use invertibility of $\rho$.

Let $a_L$ be the left-hand composite in the statement. Expand the adjunct of the actual $\pi^S$ by [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Naturality of $t_S$ in its first input, followed by (**) at $J=K$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
a_L^\flat&=(\varepsilon^S_{D_XK}\otimes1)\circ t_{S,F_SD_XK,D_YM}\circ L_S(\rho_K\otimes1)\circ L_S(b_{Y,C,M})\\
&=(D_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\otimes1)\circ(\lambda_C\otimes1)\circ t_{S,D_YC,D_YM}\circ L_S(b_{Y,C,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
The tensor maps are natural bifunctorial comparisons by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These equalities only compose the defining counit equation with the displayed maps.

Apply (*) at $(C,M)$, and cancel the invertible second component $\lambda_M$. The expression in step 5 becomes
$$(D_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\lambda_M^{-1})\circ b_{X,L_RC,L_RM}\circ D_X(t_{R,C,M})\circ\lambda_W.$$
Naturality of $b_X$ at $(\varepsilon^R_K,1)$ now rewrites it as
$$a_L^\flat=q\circ D_X\bigl((\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1)\circ t_{R,C,M}\bigr)\circ\lambda_W.\tag{***}$$
This naturality is the simultaneous naturality of the scalar pullback tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity geometric morphism with structural ring map $R_X\to S_X$.

Let $a_R=F_S(q)\circ\rho_H\circ D_Y(\pi^R_{f,K,M})$ be the right-hand composite. Counit naturality, then (**) at $H$, then naturality of $\lambda$ at $\pi^R:W\to F_RH$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_R^\flat&=q\circ\varepsilon^S_{D_XH}\circ L_S(\rho_H)\circ L_SD_Y(\pi^R)\\
&=q\circ D_X(\varepsilon^R_H)\circ\lambda_{F_RH}\circ L_SD_Y(\pi^R)\\
&=q\circ D_X\bigl(\varepsilon^R_H\circ L_R(\pi^R)\bigr)\circ\lambda_W.
\end{aligned}$$
By the defining adjunct of the actual integral projection map [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map],
$$\varepsilon^R_H\circ L_R(\pi^R)=(\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1)\circ t_{R,C,M}.$$
The last expression for $a_R^\flat$ is therefore (***). Here only the naturality and inverse Hom-bijection identities of the adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] are used.

proof.text: The Hom bijection of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is injective, so $a_L^\flat=a_R^\flat$ implies $a_L=a_R$ in $D_S(Y)$. Substituting $q,H,W,Z$ gives exactly the equality in the statement, with its specified source and target. Each component used above is natural, so the equality is natural in $K,M$. The proof used no inverse of either projection morphism, no bound on the complexes, and no properness or completeness hypothesis; $n\ge1$ and the coefficient setting are unchanged.
